overview.title: Quant·ion
overview.summary: Reads Ionic (.ion) and mzML files and turns chromatograms into numbers: noise level, baseline, peak detection, targeted quantification and untargeted feature detection. One Rust core does the work, so Rust, Python, JavaScript and R return the same results, with the same functions, arguments and options.

projects.name: Ionic
projects.description: Streamable binary format for mass-spectrometry data: lossless mzML conversion, random access, WebAssembly.

projects.name: Quant·ion
projects.description: Noise, baseline, peaks, targets and features from Ionic and mzML files.

groups.name: Files
groups.description: Open, read and write raw files: Ionic (.ion) and mzML.

groups.name: Traces
groups.description: Functions that work on one trace: a chromatogram given as x, the retention times, and y, the intensities. They need no file. To make a trace from a raw Ionic (.ion) or mzML file, use calculate_eic.

groups.name: Targeted
groups.description: For targeted quantification: you give one file and the compounds you look for, and you get one peak per compound, all from that file.

groups.name: Untargeted
groups.description: For untargeted detection: every peak in a file, found by scanning an m/z grid, and matched across files.

groups.name: Models
groups.description: Tools to load and evaluate deep-learning models stored as ONNX. Not every ONNX operator can run, only: convolution, pooling, dense layers, multi-head attention, normalization, common activations and arithmetic operations.

groups.name: Inputs
groups.description: Types you pass to the functions.

groups.name: Enums
groups.description: Fixed sets of values, written in uppercase in every language.

groups.name: Options
groups.description: One options type for each function that has settings, named after the function. Every field has a default.

groups.name: Errors
groups.description: One error for every function, with a kind and a fixed number code, in every language. Rust returns it in a Result; the other languages throw it.

entries.name: parse_ion
entries.summary: Open an Ionic file (.ion) from a path, a URL or bytes. Paths and URLs are read lazily: only the bytes a query needs are fetched.

arguments.meaning: Where the file is: a path, an http(s) URL, or raw bytes.
Optional settings. Every field and default is listed in ParseIonOptions.

returns.meaning: The opened sample.

rust.signature: pub fn parse_ion(input: impl Into<IonInput>, options: ParseIonOptions) -> Result<SampleFile, QuantionError>
rust.warning: The sample is freed when it goes out of scope, so nothing else is needed in normal use. When processing many samples, drop each one after using it, with drop(file), so its memory is freed right away instead of piling up.

python.signature: def parse_ion(source, options: ParseIonOptions | None = None) -> SampleFile
python.example:
from quantion import parse_ion

url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phenological/ion-files/main/data/aa_p21_LTR_20_b1_w20.ion"
file = parse_ion(url)
cached = parse_ion(url, {"max_cache_size": 64_000_000})
print(file)

file.dispose()
cached.dispose()

js.signature: async function parseIon(source: IonInput, options?: ParseIonOptions): Promise<SampleFile>

r.example:
library(quantion)

url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phenological/ion-files/main/data/aa_p21_LTR_20_b1_w20.ion"
sample <- parse_ion(url)
cached <- parse_ion(url, options = parse_ion_options(max_cache_size = 64e6))
print(sample)

dispose(sample)
dispose(cached)

entries.warning: The sample is freed by the library once it is no longer used, so dispose is not needed in normal use. When processing many samples, dispose each one after using it, so its memory is freed right away instead of piling up.

entries.name: parse_mzml
entries.summary: Open an mzML file from a path or bytes. It is always loaded fully into memory. URLs are refused.

arguments.meaning: Where the file is: a path or raw bytes.

returns.meaning: The loaded sample.

rust.signature: pub fn parse_mzml(input: impl Into<MzmlInput>) -> Result<SampleFile, QuantionError>
rust.warning: The sample is freed when it goes out of scope, so nothing else is needed in normal use. When processing many samples, drop each one after using it, with drop(file), so its memory is freed right away instead of piling up.

python.signature: def parse_mzml(source) -> SampleFile
python.example:
import os
import tempfile
from urllib.request import urlopen
from quantion import parse_ion, parse_mzml, write_mzml

url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phenological/quantion/main/core/tests/fixtures/api/api.ion"
data = urlopen(url).read()
path = os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), "sample.mzML")
write_mzml(parse_ion(data), {"out": path})
file = parse_mzml(path)
print(file)

js.signature: async function parseMzml(source: string | BinaryInput): Promise<SampleFile>

r.example:
library(quantion)

fixtures <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phenological/quantion/main/core/tests/fixtures"
url <- paste0(fixtures, "/api/api.ion")
data <- curl::curl_fetch_memory(url)$content
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".mzML")
write_mzml(parse_ion(data), options = write_mzml_options(out = path))
sample <- parse_mzml(path)
print(sample)

entries.warning: The sample is freed by the library once it is no longer used, so dispose is not needed in normal use. When processing many samples, dispose each one after using it, so its memory is freed right away instead of piling up.

entries.name: write_ion
entries.summary: Write a sample as an Ionic file (.ion). With no out, it returns the bytes. A path writes a file; a URL uploads it in one PUT request.

arguments.meaning: The sample to write.
Optional settings. Every field and default is listed in WriteIonOptions.

returns.meaning: The bytes when out is left out; nothing when it is written or uploaded.

rust.signature: pub fn write_ion(file: &mut SampleFile, options: WriteIonOptions) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, QuantionError>

python.signature: def write_ion(file: SampleFile, options: WriteIonOptions | None = None) -> bytes | None
python.example:
import os
import tempfile
from urllib.request import urlopen
from quantion import parse_ion, write_ion

url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phenological/quantion/main/core/tests/fixtures/api/api.ion"
data = urlopen(url).read()
file = parse_ion(data)

ion_bytes = write_ion(file)

write_ion(file, {"out": os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), "sample.ion")})
print(len(ion_bytes))

js.signature: async function writeIon(file: SampleFile, options?: WriteIonOptions): Promise<Uint8Array | undefined>

r.example:
library(quantion)

fixtures <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phenological/quantion/main/core/tests/fixtures"
url <- paste0(fixtures, "/api/api.ion")
data <- curl::curl_fetch_memory(url)$content
sample <- parse_ion(data)

bytes <- write_ion(sample)

write_ion(sample, options = write_ion_options(out = tempfile(fileext = ".ion")))
print(length(bytes))

returns.meaning: The bytes when out is left out; nothing when it is written.

python.signature: def write_mzml(file: SampleFile, options: WriteMzmlOptions | None = None) -> bytes | None

entries.name: get_scans
entries.summary: Read scans by retention time or precursor m/z. A range returns every scan in it; one number returns the closest scan, as a list of one.

arguments.meaning: The sample to read, from parse_ion or parse_mzml.
Which scans, by retention time: a range or one value.
Or by precursor m/z: a range or one value. Give rt or mz, not both.
Optional settings. Every field and default is listed in GetScansOptions.

returns.meaning: The scans found, in rt order.

rust.signature: pub fn get_scans(file: &mut SampleFile, query: ScanQuery, options: GetScansOptions) -> Result<Vec<Scan>, QuantionError>

python.signature:
def get_scans(file, *, rt: float | FromTo | None = None, mz: float | FromTo | None = None,
              options: GetScansOptions | None = None) -> list[Scan]
python.example:
from quantion import TimeUnit, get_scans, parse_ion

url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phenological/ion-files/main/data/aa_p21_LTR_20_b1_w20.ion"
file = parse_ion(url)
scans = get_scans(file, rt={"from": 2.3, "to": 2.4})
closest = get_scans(file, rt=143, options={"time_unit": TimeUnit.SECONDS})
print(len(scans))
print(closest[0]["rt"])

js.signature: async function getScans(file: SampleFile, query: ScanQuery, options?: GetScansOptions): Promise<Scan[]>

r.signature: get_scans(file, rt = NULL, mz = NULL, options = get_scans_options())
r.example:
library(quantion)

url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phenological/ion-files/main/data/aa_p21_LTR_20_b1_w20.ion"
sample <- parse_ion(url)
scans <- get_scans(sample, rt = c(2.3, 2.4))
closest <- get_scans(sample, rt = 143, options = get_scans_options(time_unit = "SECONDS"))
print(nrow(scans))
print(closest$rt)

entries.name: calculate_eic
entries.summary: Extract the ion chromatogram of one m/z.

arguments.meaning: The sample to read, from parse_ion or parse_mzml.
The m/z to extract (Da).
Optional settings. Every field and default is listed in CalculateEicOptions.

returns.meaning: The chromatogram: x = retention times, y = summed intensities.

rust.signature: pub fn calculate_eic(file: &mut SampleFile, mz: f64, options: CalculateEicOptions) -> Result<DataXY, QuantionError>

python.signature: def calculate_eic(file, mz: float, options: CalculateEicOptions | None = None) -> DataXY
python.example:
from quantion import calculate_eic, parse_ion

url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phenological/ion-files/main/data/aa_p21_LTR_20_b1_w20.ion"
file = parse_ion(url)
eic = calculate_eic(file, 260.103, {"from": 2, "to": 3, "ppm_tolerance": 10})
print(len(eic["x"]), "points")

js.signature: async function calculateEic(file: SampleFile, mz: number, options?: CalculateEicOptions): Promise<DataXY>

r.example:
library(quantion)

url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phenological/ion-files/main/data/aa_p21_LTR_20_b1_w20.ion"
sample <- parse_ion(url)
options <- calculate_eic_options(from = 2, to = 3, ppm_tolerance = 10)
eic <- calculate_eic(sample, 260.103, options = options)
print(head(data.frame(rt = eic$x, intensity = eic$y)))

entries.name: get_ion_image
entries.summary: Build an imaging map of one m/z: summed intensity at each x, y position.
entries.warning: Only Ionic files (.ion). The sample must come from parse_ion; a sample from parse_mzml gives an invalid_argument error.

arguments.meaning: The sample to read. Must come from parse_ion.
The m/z to map (Da).
Optional settings. Every field and default is listed in GetIonImageOptions.

returns.meaning: The image.

rust.signature: pub fn get_ion_image(file: &mut SampleFile, mz: f64, options: GetIonImageOptions) -> Result<IonImage, QuantionError>

python.signature: def get_ion_image(file, mz: float, options: GetIonImageOptions | None = None) -> IonImage
python.example:
from quantion import get_ion_image, parse_ion

url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phenological/ion-files/main/data/aa_p21_LTR_20_b1_w20.ion"
file = parse_ion(url)
image = get_ion_image(file, 260.103, {"tolerance": 0.05})
print(image["width"], "x", image["height"])

js.signature: async function getIonImage(file: SampleFile, mz: number, options?: GetIonImageOptions): Promise<IonImage>

r.example:
library(quantion)

url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phenological/ion-files/main/data/aa_p21_LTR_20_b1_w20.ion"

entries.name: find_peaks
entries.summary: Find every peak in one trace.

arguments.meaning: Retention times, ascending. At least 3 points.
Intensities, same length as x.
Optional settings. Every field and default is listed in FindPeaksOptions.

returns.meaning: Every peak that passes the filters.

rust.signature: pub fn find_peaks(data: &DataXY, options: FindPeaksOptions) -> Result<Vec<Peak>, QuantionError>

python.signature: def find_peaks(x, y, options: FindPeaksOptions | None = None) -> list[Peak]
python.example:
from quantion import calculate_eic, find_peaks, parse_ion

url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phenological/ion-files/main/data/aa_p21_LTR_20_b1_w20.ion"
file = parse_ion(url)
eic = calculate_eic(file, 260.103, {"from": 2, "to": 3})
peaks = find_peaks(eic["x"], eic["y"], {"min_snr": 3})
print(peaks)

js.signature: function findPeaks(x: Float64Array, y: Float64Array, options?: FindPeaksOptions): Peak[]

r.example:
library(quantion)

url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phenological/ion-files/main/data/aa_p21_LTR_20_b1_w20.ion"
sample <- parse_ion(url)
eic <- calculate_eic(sample, 260.103, options = calculate_eic_options(from = 2, to = 3))
peaks <- find_peaks(eic$x, eic$y, options = find_peaks_options(min_snr = 3))
print(peaks)

entries.name: get_peak
entries.summary: Find the one peak near rt. With a range, only rt ± range is searched; without one, the whole trace is searched and the peak is chosen by its size and its distance to rt.

arguments.meaning: Retention times, ascending. At least 3 points.
Intensities, same length as x.
Expected retention time of the peak.
Optional settings. Every field and default is listed in GetPeakOptions.

returns.meaning: The best peak near rt. No peak gives a Peak with every field 0.

rust.signature: pub fn get_peak(data: &DataXY, rt: f64, options: GetPeakOptions) -> Result<Peak, QuantionError>

python.signature: def get_peak(x, y, rt: float, options: GetPeakOptions | None = None) -> Peak
python.example:
from quantion import calculate_eic, get_peak, parse_ion

url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phenological/ion-files/main/data/aa_p21_LTR_20_b1_w20.ion"
file = parse_ion(url)
eic = calculate_eic(file, 260.103, {"from": 2, "to": 3})
peak = get_peak(eic["x"], eic["y"], 2.383, {"range": 0.05})
anywhere = get_peak(eic["x"], eic["y"], 2.383)
print(peak)
print(anywhere)

js.signature: function getPeak(x: Float64Array, y: Float64Array, rt: number, options?: GetPeakOptions): Peak

r.example:
library(quantion)

url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phenological/ion-files/main/data/aa_p21_LTR_20_b1_w20.ion"
sample <- parse_ion(url)
eic <- calculate_eic(sample, 260.103, options = calculate_eic_options(from = 2, to = 3))
peak <- get_peak(eic$x, eic$y, rt = 2.383, options = get_peak_options(range = 0.05))
anywhere <- get_peak(eic$x, eic$y, rt = 2.383)
print(peak)
print(anywhere)

entries.name: fit_peak
entries.summary: Fit a Gaussian or EMG curve to the peak near rt. rt says which peak; its apex intensity is the starting point unless you force one.

arguments.meaning: Retention times, ascending. At least 3 points.
Intensities, same length as x.
Expected retention time of the peak.
Optional settings. Every field and default is listed in FitPeakOptions.

returns.meaning: The fitted curve, or none when no peak is found or the fit fails.

rust.signature: pub fn fit_peak(data: &DataXY, rt: f64, options: FitPeakOptions) -> Result<Option<PeakParameters>, QuantionError>

python.signature: def fit_peak(x, y, rt: float, options: FitPeakOptions | None = None) -> PeakParameters | None
python.example:
from quantion import PeakShape, calculate_eic, fit_peak, parse_ion

url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phenological/ion-files/main/data/aa_p21_LTR_20_b1_w20.ion"
file = parse_ion(url)
eic = calculate_eic(file, 260.103, {"from": 2, "to": 3})
params = fit_peak(eic["x"], eic["y"], 2.383)
gaussian = fit_peak(eic["x"], eic["y"], 2.383, {"shape": PeakShape.GAUSSIAN})
print(params)
print(gaussian)

js.signature: function fitPeak(x: Float64Array, y: Float64Array, rt: number, options?: FitPeakOptions): PeakParameters | null

r.example:
library(quantion)

url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phenological/ion-files/main/data/aa_p21_LTR_20_b1_w20.ion"
sample <- parse_ion(url)
eic <- calculate_eic(sample, 260.103, options = calculate_eic_options(from = 2, to = 3))
params <- fit_peak(eic$x, eic$y, rt = 2.383)
gaussian <- fit_peak(eic$x, eic$y, rt = 2.383, options = fit_peak_options(shape = "GAUSSIAN"))
print(params)
print(gaussian)

entries.name: draw_peaks
entries.summary: Simulate a chromatogram from one or more peak shapes. Every peak is drawn into the same chromatogram; where they overlap, intensities add up. No real data is needed.

arguments.meaning: The peaks to draw, one PeakParameters per peak.
Optional settings. Every field and default is listed in DrawPeaksOptions.

returns.meaning: The simulated chromatogram: x = retention times, y = summed intensities.

rust.signature: pub fn draw_peaks(params: &[PeakParameters], options: DrawPeaksOptions) -> Result<DataXY, QuantionError>

python.signature: def draw_peaks(params: Sequence[PeakParameters], options: DrawPeaksOptions | None = None) -> DataXY
python.example:
from quantion import draw_peaks

peaks = [
    {"height": 9800, "center": 2.38, "fwhm": 0.021, "tail": 0.006},
    {"height": 4200, "center": 2.45, "fwhm": 0.018, "tail": 0},
    {"height": 1500, "center": 2.60, "fwhm": 0.030, "tail": 0.010},
]
chromatogram = draw_peaks(peaks, {"from": 2.0, "to": 3.0, "points": 2000})
fitted = draw_peaks(peaks)

js.signature: function drawPeaks(params: PeakParameters[], options?: DrawPeaksOptions): DataXY

r.example:
library(quantion)

peaks <- list(
  list(height = 9800, center = 2.38, fwhm = 0.021, tail = 0.006),
  list(height = 4200, center = 2.45, fwhm = 0.018, tail = 0),
  list(height = 1500, center = 2.60, fwhm = 0.030, tail = 0.010)
)
chromatogram <- draw_peaks(peaks, options = draw_peaks_options(from = 2, to = 3, points = 2000L))
fitted <- draw_peaks(peaks)
print(head(data.frame(rt = chromatogram$x, intensity = chromatogram$y)))

entries.name: find_targets
entries.summary: For each target, build its EIC at mz and find its peak near rt ± range.

arguments.meaning: The sample to read, from parse_ion or parse_mzml.
What to look for. A target without range searches its whole EIC.
Optional settings. Every field and default is listed in FindTargetsOptions.

returns.meaning: One Peak per target, in the same order. A target with no peak gets a Peak with every field 0.

rust.signature: pub fn find_targets(file: &mut SampleFile, targets: &[Target], options: FindTargetsOptions) -> Result<Vec<Peak>, QuantionError>
rust.output:
compound_1: rt 2.383  intensity 168984  integral 274621
compound_2: rt 1.903  intensity 136686  integral 193667
compound_3: rt 3.060  intensity 397468  integral 1105423

python.signature: def find_targets(file, targets: Sequence[Target], options: FindTargetsOptions | None = None) -> list[Peak]
python.example:
from quantion import find_targets, parse_ion

targets = [
    {"id": "compound_1", "mz": 260.1034, "rt": 2.383, "range": 0.05},
    {"id": "compound_2", "mz": 317.1250, "rt": 1.903, "range": 0.05},
    {"id": "compound_3", "mz": 188.0818, "rt": 3.060, "range": 0.05},
]
options = {
    "eic": {"from": 1.5, "to": 3.5},
    "find_peaks": {"min_intensity": 1000},
    "threads": 4,
}

file = parse_ion("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phenological/ion-files/main/data/aa_p21_LTR_20_b1_w20.ion")
peaks = find_targets(file, targets, options)

for index in range(len(peaks)):
    peak = peaks[index]
    print(f"{targets[index]['id']}: rt {peak['rt']:.3f}  intensity {peak['intensity']:.0f}  integral {peak['integral']:.0f}")

js.signature: async function findTargets(file: SampleFile, targets: Target[], options?: FindTargetsOptions): Promise<Peak[]>
js.output:
compound_1: rt 2.383  intensity 168984  integral 274621
compound_2: rt 1.903  intensity 136686  integral 193667
compound_3: rt 3.060  intensity 397468  integral 1105423

r.example:
library(quantion)

url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phenological/ion-files/main/data/aa_p21_LTR_20_b1_w20.ion"
targets <- data.frame(
  id    = c("compound_1", "compound_2", "compound_3"),
  mz    = c(260.1034, 317.1250, 188.0818),
  rt    = c(2.383, 1.903, 3.060),
  range = c(0.05, 0.05, 0.05)
)
options <- find_targets_options(
  eic        = calculate_eic_options(from = 1.5, to = 3.5),
  find_peaks = find_peaks_options(min_intensity = 1000),
  threads    = 2L
)

sample <- parse_ion(url)
peaks <- find_targets(sample, targets, options = options)

for (index in seq_len(nrow(peaks))) {
  peak <- peaks[index, ]
  line <- sprintf("%s: rt %.3f  intensity %.0f  integral %.0f",

entries.name: PeakParameters
